questions.q: Let& $\overset{→}{α} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$~ and~$\overset{→}{β} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$. Let~$\overset{→}{β}1$~be parallel to~$\overset{→}{α}$~and~$\overset{→}{β}2$~be perpendicular to~$\overset{→}{α}$. If~$\overset{→}{β} = \overset{→}{β}1 + \overset{→}{β}2$, then the value of~$5\overset{→}{β}2 \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that& $\overset{→}{α} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{β} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{β} = \overset{→}{\beta1} + \overset{→}{\beta2}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{\beta2} = \overset{→}{β} - \overset{→}{\beta1} . . . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

since~$\overset{→}{β}1$~is parallel to~$\overset{→}{α}$,~$\overset{→}{\beta1} = t\overset{→}{α}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{\beta1} = t\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) = 4t\overset{^}{i} + 3t\overset{^}{j} + 5t\overset{^}{k} . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Substituting the values of~$\overset{→}{\beta1}$~and~$\overset{→}{α}$~in~$( 1 )$, we get

$\overset{→}{\beta2} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} - \left(4t\overset{^}{i} + 3t\overset{^}{j} + 5t\overset{^}{k}\right) = \left(1 - 4t\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left($2 - 3t\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(-4 - 5t\right)\overset{^}{k} . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

since~$\overset{→}{\beta2}$~is perpendicular to~$\overset{→}{α}$, so~$\overset{→}{\beta2} \cdot \overset{→}{α} =0$

$⇒ \left[\left(1 - 4t\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - 3t\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(-4 - 5t\right)\overset{^}{k}\right] \cdot \left[4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right] = 0$

$⇒ 4\left(1 - 4t\right) + 3\left(2 - 3t\right) + 5\left(-4 - 5t\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4 - 16t + 6 - 9t - 20 - 25t = 0$

$⇒ - 50t = 10⇒ t = $\dfrac{- 1}{5}

From~ \left($2\right)$~and~ \left($3\right)$,~we get $\overset{→}{\beta1} = $\dfrac{- 1}{5} \left($4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{→}{\beta2} = \dfrac{9}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{13}{5}\overset{^}{j} -3\overset{^}{k} = \dfrac{1}{5} \left($9\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} - 15\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, the value of~$5\overset{→}{β}2 $\cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$~will be,

$= 5 \times \dfrac{1}{5} (9\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} - 15\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) =9 + 13 - 15 = 7$

$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a point on the line $\overset{→}{r} = \left(1 - 3\mu\right)\overset{^}{i} +  \left(\mu -1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left($2 + 5\mu\right)\overset{^}{k}$ and B\left($3, 2, 6\right)$ be a point in the space. Then the value of $\mu$ for which the vector $\overset{→}{AB}$ is parallel to the plane $x - 4y + 3z = 1$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $A$ is \left(1 - 3\mu, \mu - 1, 2 + 5\mu\right)$

We know that the vector joining two points~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$~and~ \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$~is~\left({x}_{2} - {x}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left({y}_{2} - {y}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left({z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AB} = \left(3\mu + 2\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - \mu\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 - 5\mu\right)\overset{^}{k}$ which is parallel to plane $x - 4y + 3z = 1$

$⇒ 1\left(3\mu + 2\right) - 4\left(3 - \mu\right) + 3\left(4 - 5\mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3\mu + 2 - 12 + 4\mu + 12 - 15\mu = 0$

$⇒ - 8\mu + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{1}{4} .

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \beta\overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$~be two vectors, such that $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{i} + 12\overset{^}{k}$. Then the projection of $\overset{→}{b} - 2\overset{→}{a}$~on $\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{a}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Let& $\overset{→}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \beta\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

Now finding~$\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 12\overset{^}{k}$

$= \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ \alpha & 1 & \beta \\ 3 & - 5 & 4\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \left(4 + 5\beta\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3\beta - 4\alpha\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- 5\alpha - 3\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$= - \overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 12\overset{^}{k}$

Now on comparing side we get,

$4 + 5\beta = - 1, 3\beta - 4\alpha = 9, - 5\alpha - 3 = 12$

$\beta = - 1, \alpha = - 3$

So,~$\overset{→}{a} = - 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

So,$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} = - 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Now finding~\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 = 11 \text{ and } \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 = 50$

And~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = - 9 + \left(-5\right) - 4 = - 18$

Now projection of~\left(\overset{→}{b} -2\overset{→}{a}\right)$~on~$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}$~will be~

$= \left(\overset{→}{b} -2\overset{→}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right)\left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right|$

$= \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 - 2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 - \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right| = \dfrac{50 - 22 - \left(- 18\right)}{5} = \dfrac{46}{5}$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}$ be a non-zero vector parallel to the line of intersection of the two planes described by $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the vector $\overset{→}{a}$ and the vector $\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 6$, then the ordered pair  \left(\theta, | \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} |\right)$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} be a non-zero vector parallel to the line of intersection of the two planes described by $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$,~

So finding the normal vector to the above plane, we get,

$\overset{→}{n}1 = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

And normal vector to planes~$\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$~will be,

$\overset{→}{n}2 = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}$\right| = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Now~$\overset{→}{a} = \lambda \left(\overset{→}{n}1 \times \overset{→}{n}2\right)$

So, direction ratio of $\overset{→}{a} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|= - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Hence, direction ratio~of $\overset{→}{a} = \left(0, - 2, 2\right) = \left(0, - 1, 1\right)$

Now given,~$\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

And~$\overset{→}{a} = \lambda ( - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} )$

So,~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} =6 = \lambda ( 2 + 1 )$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

$∴ \overset{→}{a} = - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Now we know that,~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = | \overset{¯}{a} | |b | cos\theta$

$⇒ 6 = $2\sqrt{2} \times$3cos\theta$

$⇒ cos\theta = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ \theta = $\dfrac{π}{4}

Now finding,~\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|sin\theta $=2\sqrt{2} \times$3 \times $\dfrac{1}{2} =$6$

Hence, ordered pair~\left(\theta, \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right|\right) = \left(\dfrac{π}{4},$6)$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k},$~$\overset{→}{b} = {b}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k}$ be three vectors such that the projection vector of $\overset{→}{b}$ on $\overset{→}{a}$ is \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$ . Since \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right)$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{c}$, hence

\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$

$⇒ 5 + 1 + 2 + 5{b}_{1} + {b}_{2}^{ } + 2 = 0$

$⇒ 5{b}_{1} + {b}_{2} = - 10 . . . \left(1\right)$~

Given,

$\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$

\left\{∵ \overset{→}{p} = r\overset{^}{i} + s\overset{^}{j} + t\overset{^}{k} ⇒ \left|\overset{→}{p}\right| = \sqrt{r^{2} + s^{2} + t^{2}}\right\}$

$⇒ {b}_{1} + {b}_{2} + 2 = 4$

$⇒ {b}_{1} + {b}_{2} = 2 . . . \left(2\right)$~

Solving \left(1\right)$ and \left(2\right),{b}_{1} = - 3, {b}_{2} = 5$

$∴ \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = $\sqrt{9 + 25 + 2} =$6$

$

questions.q: Let $O$ be the origin and the position vector of the point $P$ be~$- \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3k$. If the position vectors of the points $A, B$ and $C$ are~$- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3k, 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2k$~and $- 4\overset{^}{i} ^ + 2\overset{^}{j} - k$~respectively, then the projection of the vector $\overset{→}{OP}$ on a vector perpendicular to the vectors $\overset{→}{AB}$ and $\overset{→}{AC}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$O$ be the origin and the position vector of the point $P$ be~$- \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$,

So,~$\overset{→}{OP} = - \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Also given~the position vectors of the points $A, B$ and $C$ are~$- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$~and $- 4\overset{^}{i} ^ + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$~

Now finding,~

$\overset{→}{AB} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{AC} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And~$\overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ - 2 & 1 & 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC} = 5 \overset{^}{i} - 10 \overset{^}{j} + 10 \overset{^}{k}$

Now finding the Projection of~$\overset{→}{OP}$~on vector perpendicular to~$\overset{→}{AB} \text{ and } \overset{→}{AC}$~we get,

Projection$= \left|\overset{→}{OP} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC}\right)\left|\overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{AC}\right|\right|$

$= \dfrac{5\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)}{5\sqrt{1 + 4 + 4}}= 3$

Then $S$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

& $\overset{→}{u} = a\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{v} = \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2a\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)\overset{^}{k}$~

For angle to be acute~$\overset{→}{u} \cdot \overset{→}{v} > 0$

$⇒ \left(a\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) . \left(\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2a\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) > 0$

$⇒ a\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}b\right)2 - 12 + 6a \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$b\right) > 0$~$\forall b > 1$

Let~$y = a \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$b\right)2 - 12 + 6a\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$b\right)$

Now let $\log_{\mathrm{e}}b = t ⇒ t > 0$~as $b > 1$

Now~$y = at^{2} + 6at - 12 > 0, \forall t > 0$

Since~$y > 0$, so~$a > 0 \text{ and } D < 0$

$⇒ D = 36a^{2} + 48a < 0$

$⇒ a \in \left(\dfrac{- 4}{3},0\right)$~but~$a > 0$,

So,~$a \in ϕ$

$

questions.q: Consider three vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$. Let $|\vec{a}|=2,|\vec{b}|=3$ and $\vec{a}=\vec{b} \times \vec{c}$. If $\alpha \in \left[$0, $\frac{\pi}{3}\right] is the angle between the vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$, then the minimum value of $27|\vec{c}-\vec{a}|^2$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2-2 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}} \\ & =|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|^2+4-0 \\ & \because \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}| \\ & 2=3|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}| \sin \alpha \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|=\frac{2}{3} \operatorname{cosec} \alpha \quad \alpha \in\left[0, \frac{\pi}{3}\right] \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|_{\min }=\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \quad \operatorname{cosec} \alpha \in\left[\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}, \infty\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 27|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|_{\min }^2=27\left(\frac{16}{27}+4\right)=124\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The magnitude of the projection of the vector $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ on the vector perpendicular to the plane containing the vectors $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k},$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Vector perpendicular to $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$= \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}$\right| = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$∴$ Required projection

$= \dfrac{| ( 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) ⋅ ( \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) |}{| \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} |}$

$= \dfrac{| 2 - 6 + 1 |}{\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

questions.q: Consider two vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\lambda \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \lambda \gt 0$. The angle between them is given by $\cos ^{-1} \left(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2 \sqrt{7}}\right). Let \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1+$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2$, where \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1$ is parallel to \overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}} and \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2$ is perpendicular to \overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}}. Then the value \left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1\right|^2+\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2\right|^2$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\lambda \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}} \| \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}|}=\cos \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5}{\sqrt{10} \sqrt{5+\lambda^2}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2 \sqrt{7}} \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda^2=9 \Rightarrow \lambda=3(\because \lambda \gt 0) \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2 \\ & \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}|^2=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1^2+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2^2+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1 \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2 \\ & \Rightarrow 14=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1^2+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2^2+0 \quad\left(\because \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1 \perp \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_1^2\right|+\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2^2\right|=14\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 2, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 5$~and \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = 8,$~then \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right|$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 2, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 5$~

and~\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = 8$

Now,~\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|sin\theta = 8$

$⇒ sin\theta = \pm \dfrac{4}{5}$

$∴ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|cos\theta$

$= 10 . \left(\pm \dfrac{3}{5}\right) = \pm 6$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right| = 6 .$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \alpha\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, where~$\alpha \in R$. If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\overset{→}{a}$~and $\overset{→}{b}$~is $\sqrt{15\left({α}^{2} + 4\right)}$, then the value of $2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,&

$\overset{→}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \alpha\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$,

Area of parallelogram~$= \left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right|$

$\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b} = \sqrt{\left(\alpha + 2\right)2 + \left(\alpha - 2\right)2 + \left({α}^{2} + 4\right)2}$

Given~\left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right| = \sqrt{15\left({α}^{2} + 4\right)}$

So,~$2 \left({α}^{2} +4\right) + \left({α}^{2} +$4\right)2 = $15\left({α}^{2} +$4\right)$

$⇒ \left({α}^{2} +$4\right)2 = 13 \left({α}^{2} +$4\right)$

$⇒ {α}^{2} + 4 = 13 ∴ {α}^{2} = 9$

Now,~2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 + \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2$

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 = {α}^{2} + 4 + 1 = {α}^{2} + 5$

${| \overset{→}{b} |}^{2} = 4 + {α}^{2} + 1 = {α}^{2} + 5$

$\overset{→}{a} $\cdot \overset{→}{b} = -2\alpha +2\alpha -$1 = - 1$

$∴ $2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 + \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2$

2\left({α}^{2} +$5\right) - $1\left({α}^{2} +$5\right) = {α}^{2} + 5 = 14$

questions.q:
Let $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, and $\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be two nonzero vectors such that \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}\right|$ and $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$. Consider the following two statement:

\left(A\right)\left|\overset{→}{a} + \lambda\overset{→}{c}\right| \ge \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$for all $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}.$

\left(B\right)$~$\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ are always parallel

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}\right|$

Now squaring both side we get,

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right|2 = \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) + 2\left(\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right) = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right) - 2\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) - 2 \left(\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)

$⇒ 2\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) +$2\left(\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right) = -$2\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) +$2 \left(\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)$

$⇒ 4\left[\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) + \left(\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\right] = 0$

Now here given~$\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$, so

$\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a} = 0$~which means~$\overset{→}{c} \text{ and } \overset{→}{a}$~are perpendicular vector, so statement~ \left(B\right)$~is false,

Now statement\left(A\right): \left|\overset{→}{a} + \lambda\overset{→}{c}\right| \ge \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} + \lambda\overset{→}{c}\right|2 \ge \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \lambda\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) \ge \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2$

$⇒ \lambda\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) \ge 0$

$⇒ \lambda\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 \ge 0$

This~is not always true, since~$\lambda \in R$.

Hence, we can say that statement \left(A\right)$~is true and statement~ \left(B\right)$ \text{ and } is false.

$

questions.q: Let $\sqrt{3} \hat{i}+\hat{j}, \hat{i}+\sqrt{3} \hat{j}$ and $\beta \hat{i}+(1-\beta) \hat{j}$ respectively be the position vectors of the points $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ with respect to the origin $\mathrm{O}$. If the distance of $\mathrm{C}$ from the bisector of the acute angle between $\mathrm{OA}$ and $\mathrm{OB}$ is $\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}},$ then the sum of all possible values of $\beta$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since, the angle bisector of acute angle between $O A$ and $O B$ would be $y=x$
Since, the distance of $C$ from bisector $=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow\left|\frac{\beta-(1-\beta)}{\sqrt{2}}\right|=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}=2 \beta=\pm 3+1\beta=2$ or $\beta=-1$ Hence, the sum of all possible value of $\beta=2+(-1)=1$

questions.q: Let& $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{c}$~be a vector~such that~$\overset{→}{a} \times ( \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} ) = \overset{→}{0}$, then the value of~$3  \left(\overset{→}{c} . \overset{→}{a}\right)& is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{→}{a} \times ( \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} ) = \overset{→}{0}$,

Let~$\overset{→}{c} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right) = \overset{→}{0} ⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} ⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & - 2 & 3\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ - 5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} = \overset{^}{i} \left(3y + 2z\right) + \overset{^}{j} \left($z - 3x\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(-2x - y\right)$

On comparing we get,

$3y + 2z = - 5$~.....(i)

$z - 3x = 2$~............(ii)

$- 2x - y = 3$~........(iii)

On solving equation (i), (ii) and (iii) we get,

$x = $\dfrac{- 1}{6},$y = $\dfrac{- 8}{3},$z = $\dfrac{3}{2}

So,~$\overset{→}{c} = $\dfrac{- 1}{6}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{- 8}{3}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{k}

So,~$\overset{→}{c} . \overset{→}{a} = \left(\dfrac{- 1}{6}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{- 8}{3}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{k}) . \left(\overset{^}{i} -$2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = $\dfrac{29}{3}

So,~$3\overset{→}{c} . \overset{→}{a} = 29$

Note: This question appeared& in JEE Main 2022, 29th june shift 2. The question was incorrect, so it is& modified to make it correct.

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{x}$ be a vector in the plane containing vectors $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} .$~If the vector $\overset{→}{x}$ is perpendicular to $( 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} )$ and its projection on $\overset{→}{a}$ is $\dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2},$~then the value of~\left|\overset{→}{x}\right|2$ is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
A plane containing two vectors can be expressed as a linear combination of the vectors.

Hence, let $\overset{→}{x} = \lambda\overset{→}{a} + \mu\overset{→}{b} ( \lambda$~and $\mu$ are scalars$) .$

$⇒ \overset{→}{x} = \overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )$

Since~$\overset{→}{x}$~is perpendicular to~$3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k},$

$⇒ \overset{→}{x} \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + 2 ( 2\mu - \lambda ) - ( \lambda - \mu ) = 0$

$⇒ 3\lambda + 8\mu = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, the projection of $\overset{→}{x}$ on $\overset{→}{a}$ is \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\overset{→}{x} \cdot \overset{→}{a}}{| \overset{→}{a} |} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{2 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) - ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + ( \lambda - \mu )}{6} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}

$⇒ 6\lambda - \mu = 51 . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving the equations $( 1 )$ and $( 2 ) ,$~we get~$\lambda = 8, \mu = - 3 .$

Thus,~$\overset{→}{x} = 13\overset{^}{i} - 14\overset{^}{j} + 11\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{x}\right| = \sqrt{{13}^{2} + \left(- 14\right)2 + {11}^{2}}$

$⇒ | \overset{→}{x}{|}^{2} = 486 .$

questions.q: Let& $\overset{→}{a} = 6\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 12\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{c}$~be~vectors such that~$\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}$~If~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 12,$~and~$\overset{→}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 5$~then~\overset{→}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)~is equal to~_______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = 6\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 12\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{c}$~be~vectors such that~$\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}$,

$\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{b}\right) = 0$

So,~$\overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{b}\right)~are parallel vectors,

Hence,~$\lambda\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{b} + \lambda\overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} $\cdot \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} + \lambda \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2$

$⇒ - 12 = $\lleft(6\alpha +75) + \lambda\left(261\right)$

$⇒ 2\alpha +87\lambda = - 29 . . . . ( i )$

Now again using~$\overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{b} + \lambda\overset{→}{a}$~we get,

$\overset{→}{c} = \$overset{^}{i}\left(\alpha +$6\lambda\right) + \overset{^}{j} ( 11 + 9\lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( - 2 + 12\lambda )$

Also given~$\overset{→}{c} $\cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} -$2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 5$

$⇒ \left(\alpha +$6\lambda\right) - 2 ( 11 + 9\lambda ) + ( - 2 + 12\lambda ) = 5$

$⇒ $\alpha =$29$

So, 2\alpha +$87\lambda = - 29$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1$

Hence,~$\overset{→}{c} = 23\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}$

So, the value of~$\overset{→}{c} $\cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) =$23 + 2 - 14 = 11

$

questions.q:
& If $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{b}$ are unit vectors, then the greatest value of $\sqrt{3} | \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} | + | \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} |$ is
&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let angle between& $\overset{→}{a}\text{and}\overset{→}{b} = \alpha$.
So,~$\sqrt{3} | \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} | + | \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} | = \sqrt{3}\sqrt{2 + 2cos \alpha} + \sqrt{2 - 2cos \alpha}$
$= \sqrt{3}\sqrt{2 \times 2\cos^{2}\dfrac{α}{2}} + \sqrt{2 \times 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{α}{2}}$
$= 2 \left(\sqrt{3} \left|\cos\dfrac{α}{2}\right| + \left|\sin\dfrac{α}{2}\right|\right)

As~\alpha \in \left[0, \pi\right]⇒ $\dfrac{α}{2} \in \left[$0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right]

So, given expression is

$= 2 \left(\ssqrt{3}cos\dfrac{α}{2} ++sin\dfrac{α}{2}\right)
Thus, maximum value is=2\sqrt{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)2 + {1}^{2}} =$2 \times2 = 4$

$
